_comment: Every input to the break-even model. 'verified' means the number was read from the source URL on the stated date. 'assumption' means it is a modelling choice, not a quote, and the sensitivity table shows what happens when it moves.

api.note: Standard on-demand list prices, no batch or cached discounts. The cheapest complete small-model pair is used as the headline comparator because self-hosting a 0.5B model cannot be compared to a frontier model.

offers.instance: L4-1-24G (8 vCPU, 48 GB RAM, PAR-1, before tax)

gpu_rental.note: RunPod is used in the USD model. Scaleway is listed as a second data point in EUR, not converted, so no exchange-rate assumption is hidden.

owned_hardware.source: modelling choice: a used/consumer desktop with a 24 GB GPU, 3-year straight-line, load power, Ontario residential average electricity. Not a quote.

measured_power_source: modelling choice: M4 under mixed CPU load. Does not change the conclusion; it is a few dollars a month.
gpu_throughput_source: NOT measured in this project. A 0.5B model on an L4 class GPU is assumed to sustain 1000 output tokens/second aggregate across concurrent requests. Break-even scales linearly with this number; the sensitivity table is the honest part.
